note: Issue 436, natives.md sections 8 and 11. A governor at or above neutral passes a tribe's letter on before he answers it, and waits a month for the reply. Unskippable by the director's own example (the-director.md section 2): the natives are at his door and he wants orders. The reply is an Order to him, resolved by compliance into an urging on his answer; it never touches the tribe. Placeholder prose that stands in for the tribe's own words, which the Author writes.

body.text: The {param:tribe} have written to me. They object to what {param:town} is doing on ground they call theirs, and they want it stopped.
I have not answered them. I would rather answer as you would have me answer, and I think they will wait a month for it. I do not think they will wait longer.
I will tell you plainly that I do not know what they will do if we refuse them. Nobody here does.
I will tell you plainly that I have my own view, and that I am asking yours anyway.

options.text: knowing how much may turn on it
and would sooner not have had to

options.label: give them what they ask
options.text: Give them what they ask. It is not worth a war.

options.label: send them something to smooth it over
options.text: Send them something for their trouble, and carry on.

options.label: refuse them
options.text: Refuse them. The ground is the Crown's.

options.label: tell them what will happen if they push it
options.text: Tell them what the town will do if they push it, and mean it.
